conflicts.fact: Distances/numbers in the timer race and what Group C's final location is
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: straight path is 20 m, zigzag is about 30 m (different path lengths), and Group C's distance is described as similar. Lesson 2 recalls the race as both groups walking 80 m in 40 s, and says Group C had the same distance as the straight-line walker.

conflicts.fact: Which walker/group retraces steps (naming and group sizes)
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1 and 2 call the retracing walker Group C (2 learners). Lesson 5 says Data Table 1 records Walker A's displacement including a return segment, but A is the straight-line walker, and Walker C retraces.

conflicts.fact: Whether the zigzag walkers end at the same place as the straight walker in distance terms
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says Group B zigzag (30 m) and Group A (20 m) cover different path lengths. Lessons 2, 3, 6 treat the zigzag walker as having the same distance as the straight walker; Lesson 6 says the zigzag walker would show a smaller final displacement than the straight-line walker, contradicting Lesson 1 where both reach the same finish.

conflicts.fact: What the gradient of the distance/displacement-time graph gives, and which graph type was covered
conflicts.versions: Lessons 5 and 6 say the displacement–time gradient is velocity. Lesson 7 says that in Lessons 5 and 6 'the gradient of a distance–time graph gives us speed'. Lesson 8 calls the previous lesson (7) 'displacement–time graphs' when Lesson 7 was velocity–time graphs.

conflicts.fact: Kipchoge splits data: time and duration inconsistent
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 overview calls it marathon velocity splits in km/h; the data table is a 42-minute training run in m/s with checkpoints 0–42 min; the extension says velocity decreased from 5.8 to 5.2 m/s over the last 12 minutes, while the table has 5.6 at 30 min and 5.2 at 42 min (5.8 was at 20 min, so 5.8 to 5.2 spans 22 min).
Lesson 3 says negative acceleration means slowing down while still moving forward. Lesson 7 says a negative value indicates a change in direction or slowing down.

Lesson 3: boda-boda brakes from 80 km/h (22.2 m/s) to 20 km/h in 3 s on Ngong Road. Lesson 8: boda-boda brakes from 30 km/h in Kisumu in 5 s; stopping distance given as approximately 21 m, though area of triangle ½×8.33×5 ≈ 21 m is consistent, but acceleration times (10 s, 20 s phases) differ from Lesson 3 context.

Lesson 4: a mango falls 7.2 m from rest reaching 12 m/s; free fall from 7.2 m gives about 12 m/s only at roughly 1.2 s, but v²=2gh gives ≈11.9 m/s, so fine; however Lesson 4 Kipchoge runs 500 m east and 200 m west, while other lessons use his 42 km marathon as having near-zero displacement.

conflicts.fact: Where learners recorded their first prediction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 has learners write predictions in exercise books; Lesson 10 refers to their first prediction kept in science journals.

Lesson 10 matatu accelerates from 90 km/h (25 m/s) to 120 km/h (33.33 m/s) at 2 m/s², giving about 4.2 s, but the verdict depends on the truck moving; clearance given as 30 m total with 15 m truck + 5 m matatu + 10 m buffer, which is consistent; Learned lists s = ut + ½at², an equation not taught in Lessons 1–9.
